bug_semantics: With the barbuk theme active and neither CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV nor VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT set, __python_venv_prompt reads the second double-quoted field of a current-directory pyproject.toml requires-python line using awk without validating or neutralizing bytes. It echoes that attacker-controlled value as a prompt segment; __prompt-command captures the segment and appends it directly to PS1. Consequently, entering a directory containing a crafted pyproject.toml causes raw OSC/CSI/control bytes in the field to be emitted and interpreted by the terminal on each prompt render.
flaw_origin: Original pull-request member 2e53f8956f8c48b7138b556dca9b002f17d06562 changed themes/barbuk/barbuk.theme.bash::__python_venv_prompt from displaying only environment-derived virtual-environment names to falling back to pyproject.toml and added the exact unsanitized awk extraction plus echo path. The existing __prompt-command sink already concatenated every segment's output into PS1. GitHub squash f4443b147be00b0c198efcf7adbf546d761418d1 later landed the member's tree on the default branch, but the smaller member commit is the real BIC.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object names human author and committer BarbUk <julien.virey@gmail.com>; its message is 'Handle more dev tools' with four ordinary description lines and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/Bash-it/bash-it/issues/2396 identifies themes/barbuk/barbuk.theme.bash, __python_venv_prompt, the awk requires-python extraction, unfiltered PS1 concatenation, and a raw tmux pipe-pane capture showing the injected OSC bytes reaching the terminal.

First-party fix PR https://github.com/Bash-it/bash-it/pull/2397 explains the source-to-PS1 path and the final remediation. Advisory-linked merge https://github.com/Bash-it/bash-it/commit/fab8f57818f28bfc6f2a81f86a58981c4ea72e5a changes the vulnerable extraction to filter non-printable and backslash-letter escapes, removes echo -e from git_prompt_info, and strips control characters from segment output.

reasoning: The vulnerability is the new file-to-terminal trust boundary created inside __python_venv_prompt: awk treats a matching line in a directory-controlled file as prompt text, and the pre-existing segment compositor places it in PS1 without neutralization. History search first points to f4443b147be00b0c198efcf7adbf546d761418d1, but its one-parent aggregate message and PR #2367 history show it is a GitHub squash. The recoverable PR head has the same resulting tree, and member-by-member decomposition isolates 2e53f8956f8c48b7138b556dca9b002f17d06562 as the first and smallest commit that wrote the unsafe fallback. Its immediate parent directly lacks every part of that file-derived path, satisfying parent absence. The vulnerability then survives on the default branch until the advisory-linked fix merge; 7b7718c7e2a7f906e9bfcb988d547bfe0015b9e7 is the smallest direct remediation of the tainted extraction, with the subsequent PR commit adding broader defense in depth. Tag ancestry also exposes an advisory wording discrepancy: the v3.2.0 tag predates the landed flaw rather than containing it, while post-tag installations from the default branch were vulnerable and are fixed at fab8f57818f28bfc6f2a81f86a58981c4ea72e5a. Finally, the only permitted AI evidence source, the decomposed BIC commit object, has a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the causal result is NOT_AI.
